tools.why: Produces every picture this plugin makes — the poster frame, the contact sheet, the frame run behind block-graphics playback, the waveform and the spectrogram — and extracts the 16 kHz mono WAV that transcription needs. Nothing here renders without it.

Answers what is in a file: duration, dimensions, codecs, whether there is a moving picture at all. `:Media probe` is this, and every renderer asks it first — a percentage offset needs a duration, and a file with no video stream has no frame to extract. Ships with ffmpeg.

Two things, both optional. `:Media window` opens a real player window this plugin owns and can stop; and `media.audio` drives the sound for a consumer drawing its own picture, over mpv's JSON IPC socket — the clock a Lua timer cannot be. Without it, `:Media play` still hands the file to whatever the system opens it with.

Turns speech into text, locally and without Python. Needed by `:Media transcribe` and by `:Media text` on an audio or video file. A GGML model file is needed as well and is NOT installed by this — models run to gigabytes, so `transcribe.whisper_cpp.model` is set by hand and `:checkhealth media` reports which of the two is missing.

OCR for the image rows of `:Media dashboard` and for `:Media text` on a picture. Reached through images.nvim, which owns OCR in this ecosystem — media.nvim never calls it directly. Without either, image rows still appear and say what is missing.
